title: We love Bigfoot stories
excerpt: Good morning, Park County and beyond,
content:
Good morning, Park County and beyond,

Snow and cold weather hit early this week, but it’s currently sunny and warmer temps are sure to come yet.

In the news this week, we have a story by newly re-arrived reporter Lynette Zwerneman on some grant money and refurbishing that recently came to the downtown Lincoln School building. It’s a great-looking building and a fine addition to the community for its tenants and the public space available there.

Sean Batura has a long, lovely feature about Jessika Hard, who suffered a pretty serious brain injury some years back in a fall from her horse. She was a Livingston City police officer back then. But she’s back in the saddle—literally and figuratively—and we’re happy to read of her thriving. Pull up a chair and a cup of coffee and prepare to be inspired.

And who doesn’t love a new Bigfoot story? Clint Patterson, a longtime Park County resident and former bull-riding great, is the son of the man, Roger Patterson, who shot that iconic walking Bigfoot footage back in the late 1960s. You know the one—the meme of Bigfoot striding and looking toward the camera is everywhere these days.

Anyway, apparently a NEW movie, also shot by Roger, but a year earlier than the classic one, has recently come to light, and filmmaker Marq Evans has made a documentary, “Capturing Bigfoot.” He and Clint will be in Livingston Friday, Oct. 16, at 7 p.m., to screen the film at Livingston's Empire Twin Theatre. And they’ll both be on hand after to answer questions. There are a couple of spoilers Evans tiptoed around in a recent phone interview, so if you’re a Bigfoot fan, you won’t want to miss this.

Have you ever seen a Bigfoot? Might make an interesting story. Email us with your sighting or other news and tidbits at editor@livent.net.

Thanks for reading your local paper.
